job.title: Salesforce and Business Systems Lead
job.description:
• National charity supporting families with children who are ill or injured
  • Senior technical advice and support role working across a national network
  • Varied stakeholder engagement | Lead on projects | Thornleigh, Sydney


The Organisation

Ronald McDonald House Australia is a national charity supporting families with children who are ill or injured. Working across a federated network of 12 independently governed local Chapters, Ronald McDonald House Australia provides national leadership, shared services and strategic support to strengthen collective impact across the country.

Each year, Ronald McDonald House Australia supports thousands of families through Ronald McDonald Houses, Family Rooms, Family Retreats, Hospitality Carts and the Ronald McDonald Learning Program. As the National Affiliate Chapter, Ronald McDonald House Australia plays a central role in helping Chapters deliver exceptional support to families while strengthening the organisation's national presence and reputation.

The organisation continues to evolve its Salesforce and associated business systems capability, and a newly created opportunity has arisen for a technical lead to join the team.

Benefits & Culture

  • Contribute to meaningful outcomes for Australian families
  • Opportunity to support, administer, enhance and steward Salesforce and related platforms and applications
  • Lead systems improvement projects
  • Collaborative, mission-led culture with a passionate and engaged team
  • Supportive leadership committed to capability development and innovation
  • Thornleigh, Sydney | Flexible and hybrid working arrangements available


The Role

Reporting to the Business Analytics and Data Manager and fully contributing to a small, high performing team, you will act as the technical lead and primary administrator for Salesforce and other nominated business systems in the Salesforce Ecosystem. As part of the role, you will build effective relationships with key stakeholders across the nation-wide Ronald McDonald House Australia system.

You will provide technical expertise on projects coordinating with stakeholders and vendors to ensure maximum value is achieved. This will include being the lead internal resource for an upcoming project migrating from Salesforce Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) to Agentforce Nonprofit Cloud.

Skills Required

You are a relationship-focused person who enjoys managing and developing business systems which help others succeed. You have strong technical ability, well-developed stakeholder engagement skills, a strategic mindset and the ability to balance big-picture thinking with practical delivery. Comfortable working across multiple priorities and stakeholders, you can influence outcomes through collaboration, credibility and trusted advice rather than formal authority.

You will bring to the role:

  • Extensive experience administering and supporting Salesforce
  • Skills in supporting integrations and connected business systems
  • Ability to manage complex technical issues, platform enhancements and vendor relationships
  • Experience managing multiple projects and competing priorities
  • Excellent stakeholder management, influencing and relationship-building capability
  • Strong problem-solving skills using a proactive, solutions-focused approach
  • Ideally, an understanding of charitable environments and volunteer engagement

job.title: Coordinators x 2 - Counsellor or Crisis
job.description:
• Lead counselling or crisis teams supporting people impacted by sexual violence
  • Shape a high-quality clinical service during a period of growth and change
  • Senior clinical leadership role | Canberra ACT – Competitive package


About the organisation

Canberra Rape Crisis Centre (CRCC) is a non-government, not-for-profit organisation working to eliminate sexual violence against adults and children of all genders. CRCC provides free, specialist and confidential counselling and support to victim-survivors of sexual violence and their families, supporting people who have experienced sexual violence recently or in the past.

CRCC is a specialist service responding to significant and growing demand. In the last financial year, the organisation has supported more than 13,000 crisis contacts and provided counselling to approximately 5,500 clients, often with complex presentation.

This is an exciting time to join CRCC. The organisation is celebrating its 50th anniversary, undertaking repositioning and strategic planning, and developing updated models of care. By joining the team, you will play an important role in strengthening clinical practice and supporting CRCC through this next phase of growth and development.

Benefits

  • Base salary of $125,000 - $135,000 + super (expectations outside of this range will be considered)
  • Salary packaging benefits of up to $15,900 for living expenses plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment
  • 25 days paid annual leave and professional development allocation of 2.5% of salary
  • 15 days personal leave, plus access to health and wellness support
  • Emergency Contact one week per month, receive payment for 20 hours of work at penalty rates
  • Interstate applicants are welcome, relocation assistance will be considered as required


About the roles

These are hands on senior clinical leaderships roles that provide leadership, mentoring and supervision and would suit experienced clinicians who have sound clinical judgement and crisis intervention skills with strong people leadership, emotional resilience and a collaborative, team-focused approach. These roles will shape the counselling practice and crisis support teams through a period of growth and service delivery.

Counsellor Coordinator

The role will lead and support the counselling team, review cases and oversee therapeutic intervention, while ensuring a strong focus on quality assurance, professional practice and client outcomes. You will contribute to service planning, policy and clinical framework development, support staff through complex presentations and risk management, and help strengthen CRCC’s approach to trauma-informed care. You will regularly act as the Emergency Contact, providing after-hours escalation and support. The role also contributes to stakeholder engagement, professional training and continuous improvement, while maintaining a small clinical caseload as required.

Crisis Coordinator

This role supervises the crisis phone line and call-out functions and supports clinicians managing complex and high-risk presentations and ensures effective service coordination during periods of high demand. You will also oversee risk management and operational decision-making, and regularly act as the Emergency Contact, providing after-hours escalation and support. The role may also involve direct crisis intervention, supporting victim-survivors during forensic medical examinations and police interviews, and responding to disclosures of sexual violence.

Skills and experience required

You are an experienced clinician, with tertiary qualifications, who brings strong therapeutic expertise and the confidence to lead and develop others. You come from a foundation of social work, counselling, psychotherapy or psychology, and have experience working with clients that have experienced trauma. You will ideally have:

  • Strong understanding and experience of supporting people experiencing complex trauma or complex mental health presentations, including assessing suicide risk and self-harm
  • Experience providing trauma-informed counselling or therapeutic services
  • Strong clinical risk assessment and management capability including clinical supervision and people leadership
  • Emotional resilience to work with highly distressing and complex presentations
  • Bachelor of Master qualifications in social work, counselling, psychology or a related discipline with significant relevant experience


All applicants will be considered, however due to the nature of the role, CRCC is seeking a female-identifying person for this position.

If some of the criteria speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you. job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
• Last year 5043 people with suicidal thoughts contacted Lifeline Canberra
  • Partner with the board to define Lifeline Canberra’s future strategy to save more lives
  • Canberra based | Executive leadership | Mental health and community impact

The Organisation

Lifeline Canberra is one of Australia’s most successful and respected not-for-profit organisations, providing crisis support and suicide prevention services to thousands of Australians each year. Through its dedicated team of 900+ volunteers and around 20 employees, Lifeline Canberra plays a critical role in supporting those experiencing crisis, while working to create a community where no one has to face their darkest moments alone. Last year Lifeline Canberra answered over 41,000 calls from people in crisis, representing over 21,000 hours of vital phone support, all staffed by highly trained volunteers.

With a strong reputation for impact, innovation and community connection, Lifeline Canberra has built a sustainable and diversified financial base through corporate partnerships, philanthropic support, major community fundraising initiatives, retail operations and a growing training business.

The organisation’s reach now extends beyond Canberra, with operations in Melbourne (Narrm) and a commitment to increasing its impact while maintaining financial sustainability. With an engaged and committed board, Lifeline Canberra is seeking to appoint an exceptional chief executive officer to lead the organisation through a period of strategic consolidation, growth and increased impact.


Benefits & Culture

  • Lead an iconic organisation delivering life-changing crisis support services
  • Partner with a committed board to shape future direction
  • Driving sustainable growth and increased impact across Canberra and Melbourne
  • Competitive executive remuneration package including salary packaging


The Role

You will provide strategic and operational leadership, ensuring the organisation continues to deliver outstanding outcomes for the communities it serves. You’ll balance purpose with performance, bringing commercial acumen, strategic insight and operational discipline while remaining deeply connected to the mission.
Over the next three to five years, priorities will include simplifying the organisational structure whilst sustainably growing the Melbourne operation, strengthening revenue streams and positioning Lifeline Canberra and Lifeline Narrm for opportunities to increase its impact.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading the development and implementation of the strategy, in partnership with the board
  • Providing inspirational leadership to a committed team of around 20 staff and 900+ volunteers 
  • Ensuring long-term financial sustainability through diversified revenue growth, partnerships and resource management
  • Driving operational excellence through effective governance, risk management and transparent reporting
  • Building trusted relationships with community stakeholders, individual and philanthropic donors and corporate supporters, philanthropic and community stakeholders
  • Representing Lifeline Canberra and Lifeline Narrm as a respected leader in the community


Skills Required

You are an accomplished executive leader with the gravitas, commercial acumen and emotional intelligence to lead one of Australia’s most respected not-for-profit organisations.

You bring experience leading complex organisations and demonstrate the ability to balance strategic ambition with operational delivery. Comfortable working with an engaged board, you understand the importance of governance, transparency and providing high-quality information to support effective decision making, whilst having the courage to challenge constructively, providing candid advice.

You will be able to demonstrate:

  • Executive leadership experience within the not-for-profit, government or commercial sectors
  • Commercial and financial acumen, with experience driving sustainable growth
  • Experience developing and implementing organisational strategy and generating income
  • Exceptional leadership capability, with the ability to motivate, develop and inspire teams
  • Credibility representing organisations across government, business and community settings

You will know when to consolidate and when to grow, alongside a deep commitment to ensuring more Australians in crisis receive the support they need, when they need it most.

If you’re inspired to lead one of Australia’s most respected not-for-profit organisations, that saves lives every day, we would welcome your application. job.title: Head of Philanthropy & Partnerships
job.description:
• National charity keeping children safe from violence and trauma 
  • Lead philanthropy, partnerships and strategic income growth 
  • Melbourne (preferred) or Sydney | Flexible hybrid working environment 
  

About the Organisation  
The Alannah & Madeline Foundation is one of Australia's most respected child-focused charities, dedicated to ensuring children and young people are free from violence and trauma wherever they live, learn and play. Established in memory of Alannah and Madeline following the Port Arthur tragedy, the Foundation delivers prevention, care and advocacy programs, and leads Dolly's Dream to help prevent bullying and support families and communities across Australia. 

With a strong national profile, an excellent reputation, engaged leadership and a highly supportive CEO and Board, the Foundation is entering an exciting period of growth. As it approaches its 30th Anniversary in 2027, there is significant opportunity to expand philanthropic investment, deepen strategic partnerships and further increase its impact for children and young people.  

Benefits and Culture  
  • $130,000 - $140,000 + Super and not for profit packaging ( expectations outside of this range will be considered ) 
  • Hybrid, flexible working arrangements | South Melbourne office – Sydney based candidates will be considered 
  • Strong workplace culture with high staff engagement across a national team 
  • Additional gifted annual leave plus “life leave” days 
  • Commitment to learning and professional development  

About the Role  
This is a senior leadership role responsible for driving sustainable income growth across philanthropy, major gifts, trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships and bequests as well as contributing to organisation wide strategy. Leading a high-performing team and managing a personal portfolio of major donors and strategic partners, you will play a vital role in securing the funding required to expand the Foundation's impact.  

This is an opportunity for a strategic yet hands-on fundraising leader who enjoys building influential relationships, creating compelling funding opportunities and delivering meaningful social impact through philanthropy and partnerships.  
  
In this role you will also: 
  • Lead and execute the Foundation's philanthropy and partnership growth strategy 
  • Work closely with program and executive leaders to identify fundable opportunities 
  • Drive revenue growth across major gifts, trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships and bequests 
  • Cultivate, secure and steward major donors and philanthropic funders and expand strategic corporate partnerships 
  • Develop compelling cases for support, funding proposals and support major campaigns and fundraising initiatives 

Skills & Experience Required  
You are an accomplished fundraising leader with success securing significant philanthropic investment and building long-term strategic partnerships. You have a combination of strategic thinking, commercial acumen and exceptional relationship-building capability. You may currently work within a major charity, university, hospital, or sophisticated fundraising environment and are motivated by the opportunity to lead a successful and growing program. 

You will also have: 
  • Experience in managing major gifts, philanthropy, trusts and foundations, and or corporate partnerships 
  • Developed and managed donor pipelines and moves management strategies 
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement, influencing and relationship management skills 
  • Strategic planning, budgeting and revenue forecasting experience 
  • Strong collaborative leadership style, with the ability to mentor, support and grow a team  

The Alannah and Madeline Foundation is a child safe environment. All roles are subject to a satisfactory national police check and a valid working with children check.

job.title: Lawyer - Mulleun Mura Access to Justice
job.description:
• Culturally safe legal service improving outcomes for First Nations women
  • Shape a growing practice through leadership, mentorship and advocacy
  • Suits Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander lawyers with family law experience


About the organisation

The Women's Legal Centre ACT (WLC) is a specialist community legal centre committed to improving women's lives and advancing gender equality. Through legal assistance, advocacy, law reform and education, WLC supports women, trans and gender diverse people experiencing complex legal issues across family law, discrimination, employment, migration and sexual violence. WLC is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where First Nations leadership, culture and community knowledge are respected, valued and celebrated.

The Mulleun Mura Access to Justice Program

The Mulleun Mura Access to Justice (MMA2J) Program is a specialist service led by and for First Nations women. Working within a multidisciplinary model alongside, cultural support staff and community partners, the program provides culturally safe, trauma-informed legal services that empower Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women to make informed decisions and achieve positive outcomes keeping them and their children safe and connected to culture.

If you are motivated to undertake a managerial and practicing role, WLC will support your growth and work with you to shape a role that supports the legal career you want to build. This may be aspirations of going to the Bar, being a Court Litigator, time off during school holidays, exploration of a broader mix of practice areas including family, employment, discrimination or criminal law; we invite and encourage you to share your legal goals.

Benefits and culture

  • Salary range: $115,000 - $148,000 depending upon legal experience, plus super and salary packaging
  • Flexible working arrangements including hybrid and part-time options
  • Relocation support available for candidates who will move to Canberra
  • Genuine commitment to professional development, within a flexible and respectful environment
  • Annual health and wellbeing allowance, paid cultural and reproductive health leave


About the role

This is an exceptional opportunity for a talented Aboriginal and or Torres Strait Islander lawyer to join the Mulleun Mura Access to Justice Practice and help shape the future of culturally safe legal services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander women.

You will be part of a small team, maintain a complex legal case load and work closely with solicitors, cultural support staff and community partners to deliver integrated, trauma-informed services that improve outcomes for First Nations women. You will mentor emerging practitioners, strengthen relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and contribute to law reform and systemic advocacy.

You will also:

  • Contribute to strategic planning, program development and service innovation
  • Monitor program outcomes, funding requirements and data reporting
  • Represent WLC across the legal sector, community and stakeholder forums
  • Identify opportunities for collaboration, advocacy and law reform
  • Foster a positive, inclusive and high-performing team culture


Skills and experience required

You are an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander lawyer who is deeply committed to social justice, gender equality and systemic change, have experience in family law, and a genuine commitment to improving access to justice for First Nations women. You are motivated by the opportunity to work within a culturally safe trauma-informed service delivery model, and you also have:

  • Admission as an Australian Legal Practitioner with a current practising certificate (or eligibility to obtain)
  • Strong relationship-building skills with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and stakeholders
  • Experience working within or alongside multidisciplinary service models
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and advocacy skills
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage complex priorities


WLC is committed to increasing First Nations leadership across the organisation and creating a culturally safe recruitment process and workplace. Wellways works with individuals, families and communities to help them imagine and achieve better lives, advocating for change to make sure people can access the best possible care and information when they need it.
  
Operating in Australia’s eastern states and territories, Wellways, a values-led organisation provides a wide range of services and assistance for people with mental health issues, disabilities, young people, older Australians and those requiring community care.  Wellways is committed to cultural safety and reconciliation with First Nations peoples.

job.title: Country Manager, WWF - PNG Country Programme
job.description:
• Global organisation working locally towards a People & Nature Positive Pacific
  • Collaborate & innovate with communities to deliver WWF’s Strategic Plan
  • Port Moresby based; PNG nationals & Pacific Islanders are strongly encouraged


WWF in the Pacific

A People and Nature Positive Pacific will only be possible if we build it together. The Pacific region is globally significant for biodiversity. For more than 35 years, WWF has worked across the Pacific to sup-port solutions that connect people and nature, from community-led conservation and sustainable liveli-hoods to national and regional action.

In Papua New Guinea, WWF-Pacific works with communities, Indigenous Peoples, governments, and partners across the region to support community-led conservation and strengthen climate resilience. Guided by our Strategic Plan, Pacific Pathway 2030, we are working towards thriving biodiversity, elevat-ing nature, and transforming food systems across the Pacific. We believe lasting conservation happens when communities lead, traditional knowledge is valued and diverse voices are part of the work.

In Papua New Guinea, our teams work alongside communities across Madang, Central Province and New Britain, helping to create pathways for people and nature to thrive together. Whether you work in programmes, operations, finance, communications, ICT or leadership, there is a place for everyone on this journey.

The Role

Based in Port Moresby, PNG, the Country Manager provides strategic and operational leadership, guides the country programme’s strategic direction, and ensures alignment with WWF-Pacific and global priorities. The role involves high-level stakeholder engagement, fundraising and donor liaison, policy advocacy and partnership building to drive conservation outcomes.

Leading a team of close to 30 staff, the Country Manager oversees financial sustainability, operational efficiency, reporting, risk, and compliance management. Other key responsibilities include fostering an organisational culture that emphasises staff engagement, learning, innovation, high performance and inclusion, while supporting the professional growth and well-being of all staff in collaboration with the regional leadership team. The Country Manager will also bring communities, government, partners and staff together, creating space for local leadership, innovative thinking and collaboration to develop solutions that reflect Papua New Guinea’s diverse cultures, biodiversity, and priorities.
This vacancy is open to all applicants. However, priority will be given first to Papua New Guinea nationals, followed by citizens of other Pacific Island countries.

Skills Required

Ideally, you will hold an advanced degree in a conservation or development-related subject and be an influential, well-respected leader with substantial experience in senior leadership roles, mobilising teams and partners, including in PNG. You will have a strong understanding of PNG’s socioeconomic, cultural and political dynamics. You will have managed and developed programmes or institutions, ideally in conservation or natural resources, although experience in international development or related fields may also be considered. Strong expertise in programme management and in planning, monitoring, evaluation and learning would be an advantage. A demonstrated commitment to WWF’s values of courage, respect and collaboration, together with personal integrity, is essential.

You should have experience in developing fundraising opportunities that have secured restricted and unrestricted funding, including from major donors, foundations, governments and multilateral organisations. You will be skilled in financial management, budget planning, risk and crisis management and the development of funding frameworks to support financial sustainability.

You will also demonstrate strong negotiation, collaboration and influencing skills, and have built trusted networks at senior levels across government, business, non-profit, scientific and political communities. You will have a track record of leading, supporting and empowering cross-functional teams, together with a clear commitment to developing and motivating staff.

If you would like to be part of WWF’s solution to support community-led conservation and climate resilience across Papua New Guinea, and supporting a People and Nature Positive Pacific aligns with your career objectives, please submit your résumé and cover letter addressing the selection criteria, quoting reference #1461510. job.title: Head of Logistics and Operations Recoolit
job.description:
• Lead and scale logistics and operations of a growing climate tech startup
  • Fight climate change through eliminating super-pollutant refrigerants
  • Suits logistics leaders with field, warehouse, or supply-chain experience


The Organisation

Recoolit is an American climate tech startup on a mission to prevent 1 billion tCO2e of greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Since launching operations in Indonesia in 2021, Recoolit has prevented over 30,000 tCO2e of emissions and secured a multi-year contract to sell carbon credits to Google.

Recoolit’s fully traceable carbon credit platform targets ‘super pollutants’ refrigerant, gases used in air conditioning and refrigeration that are thousands of times more potent than CO2 when released into the atmosphere. Recoolit partners with Indonesia's largest companies to capture and properly dispose of these gases and is backed by veteran Silicon Valley investors.

The Role

Reporting to the COO, you will lead all of Recoolit's logistical operations within Indonesia, under its subsidiary PT Recoolit Bumi Lestari. The organization is growing rapidly and this role helps scale the five-person physical operations team: procuring and maintaining a fleet of refrigerant-recovery equipment, dispatching it on-demand to partner sites, training partners and supporting their refrigerant operations, and operating a central warehouse plus regional depots where refrigerant gas is stored and handled. What you will do:

  • Own logistics end-to-end: equipment availability, maintenance, and inventory.
  • Recruit and lead a growing multifunctional logistics team including technical operations.
  • Lead Recoolit's HSE program, promoting and implementing a culture of safety.
  • Drive operational excellence, technical best practice, and team KPIs.


Skills Required

Recoolit needs a hands-on leader with at least 7+ years of experience in logistics, field operations, warehousing, or supply-chain operations, including 3+ years managing a multidisciplinary team. You should be comfortable working in a digital-first environment, where rigorous tracking, data quality, and consistent process are the keys to success. You thrive in a dynamic start up culture and you align with Recoolit’s values: you are constantly learning, operate with transparency, take ownership, act as part of a team, and you are motivated by climate impact. Related industry (e.g. carbon markets, HVAC, real estate), products and a technical background are a strong plus, but not essential. You will also offer:

  • Strong analytical, and decision-making skills, the ability to solve complex problems.
  • High learning agility, capacity to master unfamiliar domains and establish effective processes.
  • Excellent communication skills, written and verbal, in English and Indonesian.


If you are passionate about climate and eliminating super pollutants, please submit your resume and cover letter, addressing the skills required, quoting # 1467610 to com Important: Recoolit uses Pangram, and candidates whose applications are flagged as AI-written will be rejected.

Full working rights for Indonesia essential, no visa sponsorships provided.

job.title: Consultant Program Manager Southeast Asia
job.description:
• Accelerate the clean energy transition with a top climate action funder
  • Leverage your climate or energy expertise and develop regional strategy
  • Asia-based, remote, work & residency rights required, Asian language essential


The Organisation

The Sequoia Climate Foundation is a private climate philanthropy foundation based in California. Sequoia is committed to bolstering the urgent work of the Foundation’s grantees and leveraging climate science to accelerate the energy transition across geographies and sectors.

Together with its grantees and partners, Sequoia is working towards building a world powered by clean energy, where all people are protected by policies that have averted the worst effects of climate change.

Sequoia believes that solving climate change requires the adoption of ambitious, evidence-based solutions that transform markets, advance clean technology, and lead to large‐scale change to avoid dangerous climate tipping points and irreversible damage. Sequoia supports ambitious organizations and coalitions catalyzing rapid emissions reductions, transforming global markets, and accelerating the transition to clean energy around the world.


Benefits & Culture

  • One-year initial contract.
  • Opportunities to travel and learn; work with a mission-driven global team and partners in an ambitious top climate mitigation climate philanthropy.
  • Asia-based, remote. (Indonesia ideal, Thailand, Vietnam, and Singapore are also possible). Work rights required.


The Role

Ideally based in Indonesia, this regional role leads the implementation of a regional strategy for Southeast Asia, working with diverse partners in the region to develop organizational presence, mobilize coalitions, and influence funding strategies and policy outcomes.

You will support the development and management of a grantmaking portfolio; identifying and strategizing to strengthen the institutional capacity of partners and the climate ecosystem in the region. Importantly, you will develop grant recommendations and bring stakeholders together to accelerate energy transition across Southeast Asia.

Utilizing your understanding of systemic change, your role is to leverage and scope key networks with peer organizations, government officials, civil society, and key stakeholders to assess emerging needs, gaps, opportunities, to advance grantmaking strategies and portfolios.

Strategically leveraging Sequoia’s resources, your work will drive stronger funder coordination including supporting climate philanthropy development in Asia.


Skills Required

With broad Southeast Asia experience, you have a good understanding of renewable energy systems or climate mitigation, and international and regional climate diplomacy. Ideally holding a relevant advanced qualification, you are eager to help accelerate the regional energy transition by leveraging your program management experience and your strong networking and influencing skills across diverse and senior stakeholders. You must have proven government engagement experience and the capacity to disseminate complex and technical information.

Ideally you have a nonprofit programs, international development, philanthropy, advocacy, or related background, and you are a collaborative, savvy relationship builder and confident presenter, with a demonstrated understanding of how to create systemic change. You also offer:

  • Proven capacity to develop relevant creative strategies to solve complex problems.

job.title: Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander Partnerships Manager (Identified)
job.description:
• Build partnerships with Traditional Custodians to support caring for Country
  • Protect ecosystems and wildlife through collaborative conservation efforts
  • Adelaide or within South Australia | Full Time or Part Time considered



About the Organisation
Bush Heritage Australia (BHA) is a leading not-for-profit conservation organisation dedicated to protecting ecosystems, wildlife, and cultural heritage across the continent. Founded in 1991, BHA owns and manages a network of conservation reserves and works in partnership with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and others to create sustainable, collaborative conservation solutions.

By 2030, Bush Heritage aims to strengthen a growing number of Aboriginal partnerships, double the land it owns and manages, and enhancing biodiversity on agricultural land. Guided by values of harmony, possibility, learning, and impactful action, Bush Heritage is committed to protecting Country for future generations.


Benefits and Culture
  • Salary range: $92,658 - $113,248 plus 12% super
  • Flexible work location – Adelaide or within South Australia
  • Regular travel within the SA Arid Rangelands region
  • Supportive, values-led workplace with Aboriginal leadership representation
  • Generous leave provisions (annual, family, cultural, parental)



The Role

The Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander Partnerships Manager plays a key leadership role in strengthening and growing partnerships with Traditional Custodians across Bush Heritage reserves and priority landscapes in South Australia. You will champion Bush Heritage’s commitment to a “right-way” approach to Caring for Country by fostering respectful partnerships, supporting conservation initiatives, and contributing to Aboriginal cultural capability across the organisation.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing and deepening relationships and partnerships with Traditional Custodians in the South Australian Arid Rangelands
  • Supporting reserve and landscape managers to engage effectively with Traditional Custodians
  • Facilitating co-developed conservation program and projects with Aboriginal partners, including Healthy Country Plans
  • Collaborating with philanthropy, communications and corporate teams to secure resources for partnership
  • Regular travel to regional and remote areas to build and maintain relationships


Skills and Experience

You are a natural community connector who has strong relationships within the SA Arid Rangelands, with a commitment to caring for country and nature conservation. You have experience building respectful, meaningful relationships and working alongside Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities particularly in regional and remote contexts and understand the contemporary issues affecting Aboriginal peoples in achieving cultural, social and environmental aspirations.

You also have:

  • Strong connections or understanding of Traditional Custodian groups in the SA Arid Rangelands
  • Experience in developing genuine, respectful relationships with Aboriginal people
  • Worked across government, NGOs or other sectors to support Aboriginal-led outcomes
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Managed significant projects and budgets
  • Confidence working independently and collaboratively across dispersed teams
  • A current manual driver’s licence and a willingness to travel
